newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Wessex eyed for shareholder benefit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Wessex eyed for shareholder benefit.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Wessex Water Plc should turn in higher half year profits when it reports on December 3 but the market will mark down shares if it does not offer to return value to shareholders, analysts said.
"The shares will fall if Wessex does not do something for shareholders," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
Pretax profits are expected to be between 72 and 77 million stg, up from 68.4 million stg a year ago, while the dividend should be around 5.6-5.7 pence per share compared with five pence previously.

Wessex is eyed for handing out a special dividend or making a buy back of shares after its proposed bid for fellow water company South West Water was blocked by the government in October, along with a rival plan from Severn Trent.

Severn Trent hiked its interim dividend 14 percent when it reported half year pretax, pre-exceptional profits up 6.6 percent to 201.5 million stg on November 26 and said it would buy back 10 percent of its shares.
It took an exceptional charge of 4.5 million stg related to its own aborted bid for South West Water.
Analysts said Wessex was likely to follow Severn Trent's lead but added there was a possibility it might pursue another acquisition.
"Chances of them doing nothing are about a third, there is a 50 percent chance of a buyback or special dividend and about one sixth chance they will go for an acquisition," the analyst said.
